cells.speakerNotes:
KEY MESSAGE
The case is a stakeholder-translation exercise, not a dashboard build.

SAY
"Kari asked whether storms change laser activity. Over the next 20 minutes I'll show how I turned that into a metric that can be trusted, a dbt model that answers it, and what two weeks of data honestly supports."

TRANSITION
Start with what she actually asked for.

KEY MESSAGE
"Less active" hides two different phenomena: the laser shooting less, or the node not running.

SAY
- Read the quote. Farmers have two competing explanations: equipment in rough weather, or different fish behaviour.
- The reframe that shapes everything: activity has to be split into uptime and a rate per operating hour, and we need to know how complete the reporting is.
- There is a customer meeting in a few weeks, so the output must be a dashboard Kari can drive herself, not a one-off analysis.

TRANSITION
"That's the question. Here is the data we have to answer it with."

KEY MESSAGE
Four source tables, four grains. The challenge is temporal, not volume.

SAY
- Walk the grain column: node-day, deployment interval, storm per site, fish-count entry.
- node_daily_activity has no site or pen; node_pen_assignment is the bridge, and it is time-ranged.
- Storms attach at site level; farmer logs at pen level.
- There are no site names, pen metadata or geography in the extract — I deliberately did not invent any.
- Exploration lives in notebooks/01_data_exploration.py; this deck carries only the findings that changed a decision.

TRANSITION
"Small data, but it fights back in five specific ways."

KEY MESSAGE
Every data-quality finding became a modelling decision, not a footnote.

SAY
- N05 moved S02/P202 -> S01/P103 on 8 Oct. Joining on node_id alone would credit its first week to P103.
- Missing is not zero: N05 has no record on its move day, N04 none on 12 Oct. But genuine zeros exist too — N01 and N03 report uptime 0 at the storm peak. The model must keep those apart.
- One 36-hour storm lands on three local days: 300 / 1,440 / 420 minutes.
- P102 has two entries on 8 Oct, including a corrected count. Latest wins, deterministically.
- P201's 1,852,000 count is 10x the next largest. Flag it and withhold the snapshot — never substitute silently.

TRANSITION
"Those decisions define the metrics."

KEY MESSAGE
Rates, not counts; total-over-total; missing stays null.

SAY
- Raw shots compare the wrong thing across pens with different uptime and populations.
- The period rate is total shots / total uptime x 60. Never an average of daily rates: a zero-uptime day would otherwise contribute a meaningless weight.
- Fish counts give context (P101 172k vs P103 96k) but are manual snapshots, stale after 7 days, and sometimes implausible. They are not a denominator in this build.
- Reporting completeness is reported node-days / expected node-days.
- State the assumption: activity_date is a local Oslo day, and uptime is node on-time, not proof the laser was armed.

TRANSITION
"Metric defined. Now the comparison windows."

KEY MESSAGE
The episode window is wall-clock; exposure is clipped minutes per local day.

SAY
- Three episodes: S01 5-7 Oct high (36 h), S02 9-10 Oct moderate (6 h), S02 14 Oct low (3 h).
- Before = 3 local dates before the start, during = every episode date, after = 3 local dates after the end. A partially affected day counts as during.
- Look at the chart: ST-0041 is one storm but three days of exposure, and ST-0043 ends at 01:30 local so it claims only 14 Oct.
- P202 drops out of S02 after the node move: a pen only joins an episode when it had nodes at that site on a during date.
- Reliability gate: S01 comparisons sit on 100% completeness before and during; P103's after-window is 66.7% because of the move.

TRANSITION
"Those rules live in the intermediate layer. Here is the architecture."

KEY MESSAGE
Layer boundaries are the design; each hard problem has exactly one home.

SAY
- Raw CSV -> four staging views (rename, cast, UTC, source tests) -> ten intermediate models in three tracks -> seven marts -> Power BI, Python, R.
- Staging is deliberately 1:1 and boring. Intermediate owns time, assignment, fish validation and storms. Marts are dimensional.
- Then the five ways this could go wrong: effective-dated assignment, join fan-out, local-day exposure, missing vs zero, and fish-count validation. Each has a single owner in the DAG.
- Every arrow on this slide exists in the dbt DAG; nothing is aspirational.

TRANSITION
"Let's look at what that produced as a data model."

KEY MESSAGE
Three facts because three grains; conformed dimensions tie them together.

SAY
- fct_pen_daily_activity: site x pen x date, the additive source of truth for shots, uptime and detections.
- fct_pen_storm_analysis: pen x episode x date, for the before/during/after view.
- fct_pen_storm_baseline: pen x episode, with weighted rates and percentage change.
- Why separate? A single wide fact would either duplicate the daily rows or force users to average daily rates - exactly the error we avoided.
- Point at the read-before-aggregating card: summing the storm analysis double-counts because one episode's after is the next one's before; storm_minutes is site-day repeated per pen.

TRANSITION
"A few lines of SQL show the decisions behind these tables."

KEY MESSAGE
The correctness lives in three small pieces of SQL.

SAY
- The spine: generate_series over the clipped assignment interval, then a left join to activity, so a missing day stays null and visible.
- Storm exposure: greatest/least clipping to DST-aware day boundaries, half-open interval, zero-minute rows dropped.
- The period tag and the weighted rate: total shots / total uptime x 60.
- These are excerpts, elided with ..., from int_node_days_assigned, int_storm_daily_exposure and int_pen_storm_daily_analysis.
- Tests pin them: unique grain per fact, relationships on every foreign key, a rate is null without uptime, and unit tests for N05's move and the 300/1,440/420 split.

TRANSITION
"So what does it actually say about the storms?"

KEY MESSAGE
The high-severity storm coincides with a real drop in the rate, and a larger drop in volume because uptime goes to zero.

SAY
- S01, shots per operating hour during the storm versus each pen's own three quiet days: P101 -24.0%, P102 -48.5%, P103 -8.3%.
- Detections fall similarly: -23.3%, -43.7%, -11.3%. Shots per detection stays in a narrow 1.27-1.38 band, so per-lice efficiency does not collapse.
- The uptime fact that matters: P101 and P103 report zero uptime on 6 Oct. Because the rate only counts uptime, the rate drop is not explained by downtime alone - but total shots fell much further (65% / 48% / 78%). That gap between rate and volume is the outage.
- P103 also has the node move on 8 Oct, which is why the after-window is flagged and incomplete.
- S02's milder episodes: P201 +2.6% and -3.3% - inside day-to-day noise.
- Say it explicitly: two weeks and one high-severity episode support co-movement, not causation.

TRANSITION
"How would Kari use this without me in the room?"

KEY MESSAGE
The dashboard is a decision tool, with data quality visible rather than buried.

SAY
- Four KPI cards are live from the warehouse: 34,862 shots, 1,359.5 operating hours, 25,493 detections, 96.8% reporting completeness (61 of 63 node-days).
- The layout maps one-to-one to Kari's questions: timeline with storm bands, before/during/after, pen comparison, site comparison, filters.
- A quality badge is part of the design: never show a rate without its completeness.
- Power BI model: import the seven marts, relate each dimension to each fact one-to-many, single direction, measures per fact. No fact-to-fact relationship.

TRANSITION
"What still needs checking before this goes to a customer?"

KEY MESSAGE
Tested, but explicit about assumptions and the causal limit.

SAY
- 21 models, 336 generic/singular tests and 11 unit tests: 346 pass, one intentional warn - P201's implausible count.
- Tests cover uniqueness, foreign keys, grain, ranges, null semantics, storm-day length, episode duplication and the hard temporal cases.
- Four things only Kari or the data owners can confirm: the day boundary, whether N03 was off or disabled, what "less active" means, and whether fish counts are whole-pen after transfers.
- Next: intraday telemetry for short storms, more episodes before any statistical test, site timezone lookup, and the production port with contracts and freshness.

TRANSITION
"So, to close."

KEY MESSAGE
Deliver a model that answers the question and states its limits.

SAY
- Three deliverables: a tested star schema, an answer Kari can put in front of a farmer, and an agreed next step.
- Land the line: the signal is in the data; the cause is not yet.
- Invite questions - especially on the day-boundary assumption and the uptime definition.

TRANSITION
n/a - open the floor.
